name: Dairying at Barcın Höyük, north-western Anatolia
summary: The first farmers of north-western Anatolia were already milking their herds and processing milk in pots at Barcın Höyük when they settled there, about 6600 BCE.
description: Lipid analysis of 805 Neolithic potsherds from Barcın Höyük in the Yenişehir Valley found dairy fats throughout the sequence, including the earliest ceramics of about 6600–6400 cal BCE. Bowls and four-lugged pots appear to have been preferred for processing milk. The investigators interpret four-lugged pots as specialized dairy vessels around 6200 cal BCE and infer that early settlers arrived with dairying knowledge.

impact.note: Shown for the farming communities of one region; milk products were a large part of what was cooked and a new renewable food from the herd, and the paper only suggests ('may have') that Marmara dairy traditions and vessels passed on to the Balkans, so reach and generativity take the lower score.

date.label: Early Period, c. 6600–6400 cal BCE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Dairy fats in pottery of the site's Early Period, which the paper dates to about 6600–6400 cal BCE, show that dairy products were already made and eaten at Barcın Höyük; the authors word this as 'by 6600 cal. BCE'.

evidence.supports: Barcın Höyük has shown that the production, transformation, and consumption of dairy products was already prevalent in Northwest Anatolia by 6600 cal. BCE, at the end of the first half of the seventh millennium cal. BCE (Early Period)

evidence.locator: Discussion, paragraphs on faunal remains and culling profiles
evidence.supports: The site had abundant domestic cattle and caprines. The authors infer mixed meat and milk use from sheep mortality and find no evidence of herd management that maximized milk production.

events.caveats: Early ceramics reflect processing of dairy products. The milk-producing species and the place where people learned the practice are unresolved.

date.label: c. 6200 cal BCE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: A four-lugged pot emerged at Barcın Höyük around 6200 cal BCE as a vessel type specialised for dairy processing.

evidence.supports: Overall, the four-lugged pot that emerged as a specialized dairy vessel type around 6200 cal BCE at Barcın Höyük may have become the typical dairy processing vessel during the Early Chalcolithic in the Marmara Region.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: The coordinates are approximate, entered for the Barcın neighbourhood, and should be checked against an excavation record.

Identify a source community or route with evidence beyond regional similarities in early milk residues or the presence of domestic animals. Aşıklı documents caprine management. The Barcın study supplies no evidence of direct transfer from Aşıklı, and it does not identify the source of later dairying at Takarkori or curd straining in Kuyavia.

evidence.locator: Discussion, paragraphs on faunal remains and culling profiles
evidence.supports: The site had abundant domestic cattle and caprines. The authors infer mixed meat and milk use from sheep mortality and find no evidence of herd management that maximized milk production.

research.note: The authors interpret the early ceramic residues as evidence that pioneer farmers already knew dairying when they arrived. Their animal-bone data allow mixed-use husbandry and do not establish a specialized milking herd or the origin of the milk.
